name: prism-payroute
description: Prism PayRoute decides which payment service provider should process each payment, and what to do when it fails. Each PSP × method × issuer has a success estimate that decays over time and borrows strength from its parent, and the router samples from it (Thompson sampling), so it keeps exploring without wasting much traffic. The score subtracts fees and latency. Circuit breakers stop sending traffic to a failing PSP and probe it before reopening. Bank-wide failures are recognised as issuer outages, so healthy PSPs are not punished and pointless retries stop. Hard declines (insufficient funds, wrong PIN) are never retried. Timeouts are ambiguous, so the router asks the PSP whether the money was captured before trying elsewhere, which is how it avoids double charges. A pre-route compliance gate covers sanctions, Luhn and BIN checks, card-on-file tokenisation, 3DS/AFA, e-mandate and UPI limits, data localisation and velocity. There is also an FX desk with expiring quotes and DCC comparison, plus a chargeback lifecycle with deadlines, evidence scoring and 3DS liability shift.
author: Soumya Bhandare (krishyaa06)
